title: Maddock Just Blinked: 'Shakti Shalini' Moved to January to Dodge Shah Rukh Khan's 'King' — and That Tells You Everything
excerpt: The horror-comedy franchise that never loses just decided not to fight Bollywood's biggest Christmas release. Here's what the date shift means for NRI moviegoers and the Maddock universe.
body:
When Maddock Films quietly moved Shakti Shalini from its Christmas Day slot to early January 2027, it wasn't just a scheduling tweak. It was a white flag — one that tells you everything about the kind of gravitational pull Shah Rukh Khan's King now exerts on Bollywood's release calendar.

Shakti Shalini, starring the relatively unknown Aneet Padda in dual roles, is the latest entry in Dinesh Vijan's increasingly lucrative Maddock Horror Comedy Universe — the franchise that turned Stree, Munjya, and their sequels into some of Hindi cinema's most reliable box-office performers. But even a franchise that has cracked a formula for turning folklore into blockbusters knows better than to open against SRK.

The December Problem

Here's what Bollywood's December 2026 looks like right now: Shah Rukh Khan and Deepika Padukone's King, directed by Siddharth Anand, is locked in for December 24. The film reportedly carries a ₹350 crore budget and features Suhana Khan in her most prominent role yet, Abhishek Bachchan as the antagonist, and a storyline that positions SRK as an assassin — the kind of big-swing premise that virtually guarantees it will dominate screens for at least two weeks.

Shakti Shalini was originally set for the same date. The film, directed by the talented Aditya Sarpotdar (who helmed Munjya), is a supernatural thriller "inspired by Bengali folklore" in which Padda plays both a protective spirit and a vengeful entity. On any other Christmas, it might have held its own. Against King? The math doesn't work.

The Maddock team is reportedly eyeing the first week of January 2027, which itself isn't a clean runway — Cocktail 2 may claim that slot. But early January has historically been kind to mid-budget Hindi films, especially those with strong word-of-mouth potential.

What This Means for the Maddock Universe

The delay isn't a crisis for Maddock — it's a strategic calculation that reflects how sophisticated Bollywood's release planning has become. The horror-comedy franchise has thrived by occupying windows where audiences are in the mood for fun, escapist cinema without the pressure of competing against tentpole releases. Stree 2 worked because it had a relatively clear August run. Munjya found its audience in a summer slot. Shakti Shalini needs the same breathing room.

For Aneet Padda, the stakes are more personal. The young actor, best known for the web series Saiyaara, is being positioned as the next face of the Maddock universe — a franchise that has already launched careers and could do the same for him if Shakti Shalini lands. A January release, with positive buzz built over the holiday break, might actually serve the film better than a Christmas bloodbath against the biggest star in Hindi cinema.

The NRI Calendar

For diaspora audiences planning their holiday movie outings, the December shake-up has a practical implication: King will almost certainly be the Indian film playing at your local Regal or AMC during Christmas week, with limited competition from other Hindi releases. The consolidation means better screen allocation for SRK's film in North America, the UK, and Australia — markets where Indian films are competing for the same limited IMAX and premium screens.

Shakti Shalini's January move could work in its favour internationally too. NRI audiences who've already seen King over the holidays will be looking for something fresh in the new year, and a horror-comedy with strong franchise credentials is exactly the kind of film that benefits from being the only Indian option in town.

Production on Shakti Shalini is expected to wrap principal photography by the end of May, with VFX and post-production work continuing through autumn. King, meanwhile, is further along — multiple schedules have been completed, and the first teaser featuring glimpses of Suhana Khan has already generated significant social media discussion.

The lesson is clear: in 2026, even Bollywood's most reliable franchise knows that some battles aren't worth fighting. You don't beat Shah Rukh Khan at Christmas. You just pick a different date.

King releases December 24, 2026. Shakti Shalini is expected in early January 2027.
